analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and the `stop` row of the sampling-parameters table (line 2126). The units supplied are base-side text around those regions; line 2126 is base unit :7 and is the only substantive change. The new text documents a `ReasoningStopScope` that excludes reasoning spans (Gemma 4 and `<think>` parsers) and tool-call spans from stop-string matching, and says a native block engine (diffusion Gemma) carries no scope. The doc says this is not a code change, so I checked it as a behavioural claim against the threat model. The change concerns stop-string semantics on the provider's local decode path. It does not touch the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), attestation or App Attest authorization (TB-009, TB-011), key custody (A-002, A-003), the prefix-cache or SSD cache identity (T-041), or the fan helper (TB-010). The existing documentation states that the sampler and stop settings are not part of cache identity, so the stop-scope change does not alter T-041. The docs make no claim of a new control and do not weaken any recorded mitigation. Open question for integration: the code implementing `ReasoningStopScope` (EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift) is not in the supplied evidence. A reviewer should confirm that scoped stop matching does not leak reasoning or tool text into client-visible output, and that stop-held-back text is not emitted before encryption. Unchanged here. The supplied evidence includes no source diff, so this documentation-only conclusion cannot rule out a companion code change in another batch.
